Panna Cotta

Piedmont vanilla panna cotta made with fresh cream, sugar, and gelatin.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 cups plus 2 tbsp heavy cream
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1 vanilla bean
4 gelatin sheets, or about 2 1/2 tsp powdered gelatin equivalent

Preparation

1. Soak the gelatin sheets in abundant cold water.

2. Let soften for 10–15 minutes.

3. Split the vanilla bean lengthwise.

4. Scrape out the seeds.

5. Put the cream, sugar, vanilla seeds, and pod in a saucepan.

6. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring, without boiling.

7. Once the sugar is fully dissolved and the cream is very hot, remove from the heat.

8. Remove the vanilla pod.

9. Squeeze the gelatin sheets thoroughly.

10. Add them to the hot cream.

11. Stir until completely dissolved.

12. Divide among 4 molds holding about 2/3 cup each.

13. Cool slightly.

14. Cover.

15. Refrigerate for at least 5 hours.

16. To unmold, dip the bottom of each mold in very hot water for 2–3 seconds.

17. Invert onto a plate.

Service

Serve cold, plain or with fruit or sauce as desired.

Chef's note

Do not boil the cream because excessive heat can affect both aroma and texture.

Bonèt

Piedmont cocoa custard with amaretti, ladyfingers, coffee, and rum, baked in a water bath.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups whole milk
about 10–12 ladyfingers, finely crumbled
about 1 1/2 cups small dry amaretti cookies, finely crumbled
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
1 cup granulated sugar, divided
1/4 cup espresso
1 tbsp ground coffee
2 tbsp rum
5 large eggs

Preparation

1. Heat the milk until almost boiling.

2. Remove from the heat.

3. Cool until warm.

4. Finely crumble the ladyfingers and amaretti.

5. Add them to the milk.

6. Add the espresso, ground coffee, and rum.

7. Stir.

8. Put 3/4 cup of the sugar in a bowl with the cocoa and eggs.

9. Whisk until uniform and lightly foamy.

10. Gradually incorporate the milk-and-cookie mixture.

11. Put the remaining 1/4 cup sugar in a small saucepan.

12. Heat over medium heat without stirring until amber caramel forms.

13. Immediately coat the bottom and sides of a pudding mold with the caramel.

14. Pour in the bonèt mixture.

15. Set the mold in a deep roasting pan.

16. Add hot water to reach halfway up the sides of the mold.

17. Bake in a preheated 340°F oven for 35–40 minutes, until the center is set but still slightly trembling.

18. Remove from the water bath.

19. Cool completely.

20. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

21. Run a thin knife around the edge.

22. Invert onto a serving platter.

Service

Serve cold.

Chef's note

Bonèt should set gently in a water bath; aggressive heat creates a grainy texture.

Baci di Dama

Piedmont sandwich cookies made with almonds, hazelnuts, butter, vanilla, and dark chocolate.

Yield: about 60–70 sandwich cookies

2 cups plus 3 tbsp softened butter
4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
about 2 cups whole almonds
about 3 cups whole hazelnuts
2 1/2 cups granulated sugar
1 vanilla bean
about 1 1/2 cups finely chopped dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 340°F.

2. Spread the almonds and hazelnuts on a baking sheet.

3. Toast for 8–10 minutes.

4. Cool completely.

5. Rub the hazelnuts in a kitchen towel to remove as much skin as possible.

6. Grind the almonds and hazelnuts finely with some of the sugar, pulsing so they do not release excessive oil.

8. Add the remaining sugar and seeds from the vanilla bean.

17. Melt the chocolate over a water bath.

18. Put a small amount of chocolate on the flat side of half of the cookies.

19. Sandwich with the remaining cookies.

20. Let the chocolate crystallize.

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Grinding the nuts with some of the sugar helps prevent them from turning into an oily paste.

Gianduiotti

Turin chocolates made with Piedmont hazelnuts, dark chocolate, powdered sugar, and cocoa butter.

Yield: about 30 pieces

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups toasted peeled hazelnuts
about 1 cup finely chopped 70% dark chocolate
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp powdered sugar
1/3 cup cocoa-butter wafers
1 pinch fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the hazelnuts and powdered sugar in a food processor.

2. Process for several minutes, stopping occasionally to scrape the sides.

3. Continue until the hazelnuts release their oil and form a very smooth paste.

4. Finely chop the chocolate.

5. Put it with the cocoa butter in a heatproof bowl.

6. Melt over a water bath to about 113°F.

7. Remove from the heat.

8. Mix in the hazelnut paste and salt.

9. Stir until completely uniform.

10. Cool the mixture while stirring to 82–84°F.

11. Gently rewarm to about 88°F.

12. Pour into traditional boat-shaped molds.

13. Tap the mold lightly on the counter to release air bubbles.

14. Let crystallize at room temperature for at least 1 hour.

15. Unmold gently.

Service

Store and serve at cool room temperature.

Chef's note

A perfectly smooth hazelnut paste is essential for the melting texture of traditional gianduiotti.

Langhe Hazelnut Cake

Flourless Piedmont cake made with toasted hazelnuts, eggs, and sugar.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

4 large eggs
1 1/2 cups toasted hazelnuts
1 cup granulated sugar
1 pinch fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Line the bottom of a 9-inch cake pan with parchment.

3. Finely grind the hazelnuts without turning them into nut butter.

4. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

5. Put the whites in a perfectly clean bowl.

6. Add the salt.

7. Beat to stiff peaks.

8. In another bowl, beat the yolks with the sugar for 4–5 minutes, until pale and fluffy.

9. Mix in the ground hazelnuts.

10. Fold in one-third of the beaten whites to lighten the mixture.

11. Gently fold in the remaining whites in two additions.

12. Pour into the pan.

13. Smooth gently.

14. Bake for 30–35 minutes.

15. Test with a toothpick.

16. Cool completely before unmolding.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Gentle folding is essential because, without flour, the whipped egg whites provide the cake's lift and structure.

Yield: 10 servings

Ingredients

10 egg yolks
1/2 cup plus 1 1/2 tbsp granulated sugar
2/3 cup Moscato d'Asti

Preparation

1. Prepare a water bath with hot water that is not boiling vigorously.

2. Put the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl.

3. Whisk for 4–5 minutes, until pale and foamy.

4. Gradually add the Moscato d'Asti while continuing to whisk.

5. Set the bowl over the water bath without letting its bottom touch the water.

6. Whisk constantly.

7. Cook gently until the zabaglione increases in volume, becomes foamy, and is thick enough for the whisk to leave a visible trail, about 8–12 minutes.

8. Remove immediately from the heat.

9. Whisk for another 30 seconds to even out the temperature.

Service

Serve warm in small dishes or over hazelnut cake, with amaretti if desired.

Chef's note

Keep the water bath gentle because excessive heat coagulates the yolks and makes the zabaglione grainy.

Preparation

1. Put the raisins in a bowl.

2. Add the rum.

3. Soak for about 2 hours.

4. Dissolve the yeast and 1 tablespoon of the sugar in 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon milk.

5. Put about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour in a bowl.

6. Add the yeast milk.

7. Mix into a soft starter.

8. Cover.

10. Put the remaining flour in a large bowl.

11. Add the starter.

12. Add the remaining milk, olive oil, softened butter, cream, 2 beaten eggs, lemon zest, salt, and remaining sugar.

13. Knead until smooth and elastic.

14. Cover.

15. Let rise until doubled.

16. Work in the raisins and any unabsorbed rum.

17. Shape into a round loaf.

18. Put on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Let rise for another hour.

21. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

22. Beat the remaining egg.

23. Brush the top.

24. Bake for about 60 minutes.

25. Test with a skewer.

26. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Slice and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Add the raisins only after the first full rise so they do not weigh down the dough during its early development.

Friulian butter-and-vanilla cookies shaped into their characteristic letter S.

Yield: about 25 cookies

Ingredients

1 2/3 cups pastry flour
1 large egg, room temperature
7 tbsp softened butter
1/2 cup granulated sugar
1/4 tsp baker's ammonia
seeds from 1/2 vanilla bean
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the softened butter, sugar, vanilla, salt, and baker's ammonia in a mixer bowl.

2. Beat with the paddle or whisk attachment until soft and creamy.

3. Beat the egg lightly with a fork.

4. Add it gradually to the butter mixture.

5. Let each addition absorb before adding more.

6. Add all of the flour.

7. Mix briefly only until absorbed.

8. Flatten the dough.

9. Wrap in plastic.

10. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

11. Preheat a conventional oven to 340°F.

12. Divide the dough into about 25 equal pieces.

13. Roll each piece into a rope.

14. Bend each rope into the characteristic S shape.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Flatten slightly.

17. Bake for about 15 minutes, until golden.

18. Transfer to a rack.

19. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long cold rest makes the dough easier to shape while helping the cookies hold their form in the oven.

Favette Triestine

Trieste almond sweets in three colors and flavors: vanilla, rose, and chocolate.

Yield: about 36 pieces

Ingredients

2 cups finely ground blanched almonds
1 cup all-purpose flour
3 large egg whites
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract or seeds from 1/2 vanilla bean
2 tbsp white rosolio
3 drops rose oil or 1 tsp rose water
2 tbsp alkermes liqueur
about 1/3 cup finely grated dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Grind the almonds finely.

2. Spread them on a tray.

3. Let them air-dry for 2 days.

4. Preheat the oven to its lowest setting, about 175–195°F.

5. Put the flour in a large bowl.

6. Add a small amount of egg white.

7. Stir into a smooth paste.

8. Gradually add the remaining egg whites.

9. Add the sugar little by little.

10. Add the ground almonds.

11. Mix until light and foamy.

12. Divide the mixture into 3 equal portions.

13. Add the vanilla and white rosolio to the first portion.

14. Add the rose oil or rose water and alkermes to the second.

15. Add the grated chocolate to the third.

16. Shape into small oval bean-shaped sweets with slightly damp hands.

17. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Dry in the barely warm oven for 20–30 minutes without browning.

19. Turn off the oven.

20. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Favette should dry rather than bake, so keep the oven barely warm and do not let them brown.
